reasons: Listing both separately and as a bundle provides flexibility for customer preferences.
Bundling can attract customers looking for a comprehensive solution.
Separate listings allow for targeted marketing to specific needs.
Etsy's keyword and page count preferences can be leveraged with multiple listings.
risks: Increased listing fees on Etsy for multiple listings.
Potential complexity in managing multiple product listings.
Risk of cannibalization between separate and bundled sales.
out.first_test: Measure conversion rates for separate and bundled listings to determine customer preference.
out.what_would_change_my_mind: If separate listings significantly underperform compared to the bundle, reconsider strategy.

reasons: The shop has no sales, reviews, or audience data, so adding a third listing tests nothing useful yet.
The Debt Payoff Planner is already inside the Money Reset Kit at $28, so a Daily+Debt bundle would overlap with it and could cannibalise that sale.
Two separate products keep the habit product (Daily) and calculation product (Debt) distinct, and the Daily Planner's weeks 14 to 16 can point readers to the spreadsheet without a bundle.
Skipping the bundle avoids extra Etsy listing fees until there is evidence a bundle adds value.
risks: Without a bundle, a buyer who wants both may not find or buy the second product, so some combined demand goes unserved.
Pricing both products at full test prices may still sit well above bestseller ranges, and a new shop may struggle regardless of structure.
If the owner later wants a bundle discount, the studio rule means both parts must already be listed separately at those prices, so the bundle price must be planned from the start.
out.first_test: Measure view-to-sale conversion for the Daily Planner at $17 against one lower step (about $14), with at least 20 views per price step, and if the lower price converts markedly better, adjust the Daily price before adding any bundle.
out.what_would_change_my_mind: If buyers of the Daily Planner repeatedly ask for or purchase the Debt spreadsheet alongside it, or Gumroad data shows a clear combined-purchase pattern, I would switch to C with a bundle priced below the sum of the parts.

reasons: The Daily Planner's weeks 14-16 send readers to the spreadsheet, so the two products are a natural pair and a bundle has a clear buyer.
Listing both products separately satisfies the studio rule, so a bundle discount can be advertised.
Keeping the separate products lets the shop test each one on its own before bundling them.
Both files fit Etsy limits: the 17 MB planner is under 20 MB, and two files are well under the five-file cap.
risks: A third listing adds Etsy listing fees and splits early traffic across three products in a shop with no reviews.
The Debt Payoff Planner already sits inside the $28 Money Reset Kit, so the new bundle could cannibalise it or confuse buyers.
Bundle price of $29 is an untested assumption, and the bundle could sell below the separate products or add little margin.
out.first_test: Measure whether the Daily Planner at $17 gets at least 20 views and any sales on Gumroad before changing prices; if it gets no sales after 20 views, the separate-product test has failed and A or a single-product listing should replace C.
out.what_would_change_my_mind: If the Money Reset Kit already sells the Debt Payoff Planner well, or if the shop can't afford a third listing, I would switch to A and skip the bundle.
